points.description: States that the principal mechanism is bio-filtration (biological action/removal by microorganisms), not mere physical straining or sedimentation.
points.partial_credit: Half only if biological action is clearly stated but the term bio-filtration is not used and the description is imprecise (e.g. 'microorganisms remove particles').

points.description: States that microorganisms form a thin biological layer at the sand-water interface, named the schmutzdecke (hypogeal layer), which removes viruses and bacteria/particulates.
points.partial_credit: Half if the thin layer on top of the sand is correctly named (schmutzdecke/hypogeal layer) but its location or its removal of viruses and bacteria is not stated.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the term bio-filtration (biological action) and the schmutzdecke/hypogeal layer at the sand-water interface removing bacteria and viruses. Vague answers such as 'filtration through sand', 'straining', or 'sedimentation' earn nothing for that point. A wrong mechanism stated alongside the correct one (e.g. saying straining is the principal mechanism) costs the point affected.
